about.title: About {site}
about.body_html:
{site} is a free lookup tool for the 2,136 jōyō kanji — the set taught through Japanese schooling. Search any character (or an English meaning, or a reading) and you get its component breakdown, its meanings and on’yomi / kun’yomi readings, an animated stroke-order diagram, common words that use it, related kanji, and a short plain-language account of how the shape came to carry the meaning.

It exists because that last part — the origin story — is usually the hard bit to find. Stroke order and readings are everywhere; a one-paragraph explanation of why 明 is a sun beside a moon, or that the 青 in 清 is a sound hint rather than a meaning, is not. {site} pulls the structural data from open datasets (KanjiVG, KANJIDIC2, JMdict, KRADFILE — see the credits) and pairs each character with a generated, plain-language etymology so the whole picture sits on one page.

It’s a reference, not a course: no accounts, no lessons, no quizzes, no progress tracking. The origin explanations are machine-generated and may contain errors.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.body_html:
{site} is a static reference site. It has no user accounts and does not ask you for any personal information. This page explains what that means in practice.

What we collect today

  • Nothing that identifies you. There are no sign-ups, no logins, and no forms.
  • Your theme and language preference are stored in your browser (localStorage / a cookie). They stay on your device.
  • Standard server logs. Like almost any website, the server may briefly record request data such as your IP address, the page requested, and your browser’s user-agent string, for security and debugging.
  • Offline caching. A service worker stores copies of pages and assets in your browser cache so visited pages load without a connection. This data stays on your device.

Advertising

{site} displays ads through Google AdSense to cover hosting costs. Google and its partners may use cookies and similar technologies to serve and measure ads, including ads based on your prior visits to this and other sites. That data is collected and controlled by Google, not by {site}.

You can review and control ad personalisation at myadcenter.google.com, and opt out of personalised advertising from many providers at optout.aboutads.info or youronlinechoices.eu. More detail is in Google’s “How Google uses information from sites that use our services”.

Analytics

None at present.

Data sources

The kanji data comes from public, freely-licensed datasets (listed on the credits page). No information about you is sent to those projects.

Children

The site is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect information from them.

Contact

Questions about privacy: {email}.
credits.title: Credits & licences
credits.intro_html: {site} is built entirely from freely-licensed data. Because KanjiVG is share-alike (CC BY-SA), this site’s derived database and pages are offered under CC BY-SA as well.
credits.kanjivg_desc: Stroke-order paths and component / radical decomposition.
credits.kanjidic_desc: Meanings (English, French, Spanish, Portuguese), on’yomi / kun’yomi readings, stroke counts, radical numbers, grade and frequency.
credits.kanjidic_skip_note_html: The SKIP code field in KANJIDIC2 is licensed CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial) and is deliberately not used anywhere in this project.
credits.jmdict_desc: Example words (jukugo) — the common words shown on each kanji page, with readings and glosses.
credits.krad_desc: Kanji ↔ component decomposition — powers the radical picker and the “shares components” links.
credits.krad_note_html: JMdict, KRADFILE and RADKFILE are used here via the JSON conversion published by jmdict-simplified (scriptin).
credits.origin_desc: The plain-language origin explanations are generated by Anthropic’s Claude (Haiku) from the component and meaning data above. They are convenience summaries, not scholarship, and may be wrong.
credits.wanakana_html: WanaKana (MIT) converts romaji search input to kana.
